data.translation: «Üh» sagte sie «mögest du mich begraben, wir machten Essen für die ganze Stadt, die Kessel sind voll, wir haben die ganze Stadt satt gemacht, du bist doch Sohn des Königs und Reich».

data.turoyo: Ŭ hawxa maʕəmriwa ab+bote, ŭ howanwa qawye ġắlabe, yani, i+kefo kuyo ... hiya ŭ hənnək ḥḏo. Ínaqqa dhowən sawiʕe xud məḷḷi, lo+gnəfli, yani, nfolo layt.
data.translation: And like so, they would build the houses, and they were very strong, like, the stone becomes ... it and they are one. If they become saturated, as I said, they will not collapse, like, there is no collapse.

summary: Remove the duplicated subject in “Er setzte der ihm”.
before: Er setzte der ihm Essen vor

summary: Restore the missing preposition in “is put it”.
before: is put it, into the mortar
after: is put into it, into the mortar
rationale: The passive clause “an excess (of kalšo) is put it” lacks a preposition. The supplied Turoyo d-mitaḥat eba expresses being put in it; the following “into the mortar” specifies the location.

summary: Restore “becomes” in the final clause.

summary: I normally codes the experiencer as subject. m- introduces a source/content (money, seeing, company, conversation); bare laḥmo, remune and šanṯo name what one has enough of. III takes an affected-person suffix or full patient NP and may add bare food/water.

Preterit Intransitive marks attained satiety, including after hul d- with prospective reference. Part act. has state predicates, explicit copulas and attributive use; do not classify solely from English 'is full'.

III Detransitive removes the feeder and profiles material saturation. MAC 84 is already quoted under Malfono_İshaq;66; do not duplicate it. The inherited form-only Mtaswaʕ is retained without inventing a full context.
The existing Preterit Intransitive cell has five examples; additions there are restricted to unusual Sawiʕutu. Repeated Joseph and bird formulas are not multiplied.
Sleep expressions and visual satiety are already covered. No newly established idiom requires addition to Idiomatic phrases.
The compact records PrS 70/48 sawəʕ and 56/118 sawəʕ lack both full verse and edition translation; can editors supply them for independent checking?
Is swóʕo in MAC NE Interview 2/165 a productive Infinitiv or lexicalized noun 'plenty'? Filing here is provisional.
What material is sawiʕo/sawiʕe in MAC Ishaq 84,86 precisely predicated of, and is 'saturated' the intended craft term?
Confirm sawiʕe wayna at Hors 2/87 against variants quoted under other roots; the supplied e supports Part act., not Preterit-wa.
Confirm Sawiʕutu in 58/229 as local morphology rather than transcription variation.
Confirm sowaʕwo in PrS 86/52 as Infectum-wa; retain the supplied o-vocalism.
Does ṣowəʕ in PrS 74/72 reflect emphatic pronunciation or transcription? Meaning is satiety, not dyeing.
Correct “strenghth” to “strength”.
rationale: The English noun strength is misspelled with an extra h.

summary: Financial sufficiency and affluent households remain within inherited figurative satiety; fire and a filled shoe are inanimate metaphorical subjects.
Mortar/buildings are described as saturated, alongside III Detransitive saturation. Keep participant extension rather than an independent craft sense pending terminology confirmation.
City denotes its inhabitants, and water can replace food as the satiating content.
